title: Proton pump inhibitors and the risk of hospitalisation for community-acquired pneumonia: replicated cohort studies with meta-analysis
authors: Filion KB, Chateau D, Targownik LE, Gershon A, Durand M, Tamim H, et al.
population: New users of NSAIDs aged 40 years or older in eight databases (six Canadian provinces, US MarketScan, UK General Practice Research Database); 2.3% also started a PPI
funder: CNODES is a collaborating center of the Drug Safety and Effectiveness Network (DSEN), funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (Grant Number DSE-111845). The funding source was not involved in the writing of the manuscript or the decision to submit it for publication.
authorConflicts: PE received speaker fees and sat on advisory boards for AstraZeneca, Boehringer Ingelheim, GlaxoSmithKline, Merck, Novartis and Nycomed before January 2012; LET received speakers' fees from Pfizer Canada and sat on advisory boards for AstraZeneca Canada, Janssen Canada and Merck Canada.
result: Cumulative 6-month incidence of hospitalisation for community-acquired pneumonia 0.17% among patients prescribed a PPI and 0.12% among unexposed patients; after high-dimensional propensity score adjustment, aOR 1.05 (95% CI 0.89 to 1.25); H2-receptor antagonists aOR 0.95 (0.75 to 1.21).
